data.translation: Wenn er sie ausgepresst hat, fließt ihr Saft, der süße Traubensaft in die Kelter.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/49)

data.turoyo: Dam mazrona məd maṭən aʕ ʕənwe, kəzze more du karmo kquṭaffe, kuwele, ksamle maḥṣarto ste bu karmo, kmaləmme l feme di maḥṣarto, w kmanṭe kiso, kul naqqa kmole u kisawo w ksoləq, kmašəġ raġloṯe w ksoləq ʕal riše du kisawo, bdele kʕuṣarre.
data.translation: Wenn die mazrona-Trauben reif geworden sind, geht der Weinberg- besitzer und pflückt sie, und er errichtet eine Kelter im Weinberg. Er sammelt (die Trauben) direkt bei der Kelter, holt einen Stoffsack und füllt immer wieder diesen Sack und steigt darauf. Er wäscht sich die Füße und steigt auf diesen Sack und beginnt (die Trauben) auszupressen.

rationale: Fills Infectum sense 1; self-contained grape pressing sequence with foot preparation and sack.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Lahdo The ḥalile/1)

data.turoyo: annaqqa uʕdo gәqqutfina aʕ ʕәnwe, aʕ ʕәnwani. gәmṭinalle lu bayto gd… gʕuṣrinalle gmaḥtinalle ʕal i nuro gdәmkawtinanne ksayminanne ʕal u falgo. falgayye gәzze aʕlayye. gmaršḥinalle hul d owәn bu falgo. qošxane gmolinala, gmarsiḥina i qošxanayo d… d nuqṣo. am mayanәk gnuqṣi gduyo bu falgo.
data.translation: So now we will pick the grapes, these grapes. We will take them home, press them, put them on the fire and simmer them until they become half. Half of them goes away. We boil them until half of them remains. We fill a kettle, boil that kettle until its contents decreases. That water (grape juice) will decrease and the kettle becomes half filled.

rationale: Fills Infectum sense 1; first-person plural grape pressing before reduction for ḥalile.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC Ishaq Material culture/119)

data.translation: I. Where do you press them?

rationale: Fills Infectum sense 1; second-person plural and object suffix in a short question.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Famine/7)

data.turoyo: <...> Ad+dawġanək gəmšaḥnínanne ŭ maḥtíwayna u+ǧaǧqawo bu+kiso, xud uʕdo d̥komaḥtina i+gweto bu+kiso, ŭ ʕəsrínanne, hul dnəšfo. Edi, uʕdo kosaymínala šərṫān.
data.translation: This buttermilk, we boiled it and we used to put that cacık into the pouch, like now when we put cheese into the pouch, and squeeze it, until it becomes dry. Thereupon we make it into kashk patties.

rationale: Fills Infectum sense 1 to five; curd processing parallels inherited cheese pressing and retains plain s.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/120)

data.turoyo: <...> Mi+šeno, ʕaməqto taḥta di+arʕo, mətro ʕaməqto ŭ mi+šènoyo, ŭ ʕuṣríwanne, ŭ kə́twayla lalʕal xud i+ṣəfro kefo, ʕuṣriwa aʕla bu+kiso, dăwamli bu+kiso ŭ bi+raġlo, dyošo bi+raġlo hul dnuḥtiwa am+maye kulle laltaḥ. Bi+ʕàrwowe bak+karme.
data.translation: Out of rock, deep under the ground, it’s a meter deep, and out of rock, and they would press them, and it had down below a stone like a platter, they would stomp onto it with a sack, continuously with the sack and the foot, treading by foot until all the juice would go down below. It was by basin in the vineyards.

rationale: Fills Infectum-wa sense 1; object-indexed and object-omitted pressing occur together with explicit foot and sack means.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/123)

data.turoyo: Elo yani šəkl qəštonóyoyo, tre+mətrowat yarixo. Dəmmina, maṯlo mu+qurmo di+dawmo, ḥub̝̊šiwa gawa di+dawmo, kule, dawmo duyo sawto. Dawmo duyo maṯe, tlōṯmó+əšne, našifo yăda quṭʕila. Saymíwayla dălāv; gawa kule maydíwayle; fāšwa u+qayso baroyayḏa; kule əzzáwayle; gəmḥalqíwayle; fāšwa u+qayso dlarwal. Ánnaqqa hánoste ʕuṣriwa aʕle.
data.translation: But, like, it’s a bow shape, two meters long. Let’s say, for example, from the tree stump, they would dig out the tree’s insides, all of it, a tree that would be old. A tree that would be two hundred, three hundred years old, it dried up, or they cut it down. They would make it a trough; all its insides, they would take; its external wood would stay; all of it (i.e., the insides) would go away; they would throw it away; the wood from outside would stay. Now then, so this one they would stomp on.

rationale: Fills Infectum-wa sense 1 to five; wooden trough as pressing surface.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.50/2341)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Maḥtiwo ʕal femayye ʕarnoṣe laǧan d l əxli. Lašan d lə moḥən femayye bu zad d əxli. ʕArnoṣe ʕəṣriwo, kətwolle ʕarnoṣe maḥtiwonne ʕal femayye maṣriwonne baq qarnaṯṯe hul d marfalle, məd manfaqqe mi draxṯo, fətḥiwo aʕ ʕarnoṣanək. Eeee d lowe manək, lə kkərxiwo gəd əxliwo u məklo d ʕal i adro.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: They would put muzzles on their mouths so that they would not eat. So that they would not put their mouths into the grain and eat. They would fasten muzzles; they had muzzles they would put on their mouths and tie to their horns until they released them. When they took them out of the threshing heap they would open those muzzles. Yes, if those were not there, they would not go round; they would eat the food on the threshing floor.

rationale: Only attestation of technical subsense 1b; retain the tying-to-horns context to justify tightening rather than liquid extraction.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.10/2303)

data.turoyo: Umarno: "Mən farq kit bayn lu ḥamro w lu dibəs?" Omər: "Qay?" Umarno: "Hano kʕəṣratle maʕ ʕənwe w hano kʕəṣratle maʕ ʕənwe, latyo hawxa?"
data.translation: I say, “What difference is there between wine and grape syrup?” He says, “Why?” I say, “This you squeeze from grapes and this you squeeze from grapes; is that not so?”

rationale: Distinct product-object and m-source frame, with both wine and syrup explicitly contrasted; the paired tokens form one example.

summary: All secure active uses fit sense 1 keltern, ausquetschen, zwängen. Grapes, medicinal plant material and cheese/curds are material variants of pressing, without a new technical sense for each product.

The Detransitive is newly attested in Infectum-wa məʕ̥ṣoriwa and Preterit əʕṣiri hani. Active generic human subjects in koʕәṣrәnne (Lahdo) are not Detransitive simply because the English says “is squeezed”.
Infinitiv ʕ̥ṣoro/ʕ̥soro denotes the process. Part act. u+ʕaṣoro denotes the worker who climbs onto the sack; keep the vocalic contrast and query lexical status.

Valency alternates explicit grapes, plural object suffixes, omitted material, and product/juice metonymy. b- names means or location, ʕal the pressing surface; inherited 57/176 has a goal in the eyes. These are not independent constructions with changed meanings.
Cross-text ʕ/ḥ and ṣ/s variants cannot be silently standardized. ḥṣr 1 is an overlapping variant entry, and initial consonant is insufficient to establish two meanings or two historical verbs.
Jan English is machine translation [MT]; the muzzle subsense is based on ʕarnoṣe, mouths, horns and subsequent tying/opening, not on the translated fasten alone.
All grape and juice uses remain I.1, with ordinary active morphology. No Jan occurrence requires a new Detransitive sense or box; round-1 Detransitive proposals are retained only as baseline.
Collective u ʕamo alternates with singular ʕuṣarwo and plural ʕəṣriwo (Jan 1.17/908–909). Do not infer separate senses from collective agreement or normalize the source vowels.

The full ordinary Infectum and Infectum-wa cells after round 1 are not refilled from the reader’s original-entry counts. Additions are the new tightening subsense and a distinctive product-plus-source frame.
The ʕṣr/ḥṣr 1 overlap was already documented in round 1; this round does not repeat the duplicate-entry proposal or change the other root. Jan ʕ-initial tokens are retained as supplied.
Should ʕṣr and ḥṣr 1 be combined or retained as explicit dialectal variants? The crossed forms already present need a consistent editorial account.
Resolve əʕṣirənxu (MAC Ishaq Material culture/125) and confirm ʕṣərile (/JTM 1.1/50) patient/agent segmentation. The former has been withheld from a definite box.
Confirm whether u+ʕaṣoro is a productive Part act. or a lexical worker term; the entry marks the attestation but does not reconstruct additional forms.
Does the plain s in Lahdo ʕusri and MAC ʕ̥soro represent pronunciation or transcription? Identify the metonymic -le referent in Lahdo The bastiq/1.
The edition says bi+ìḏo “by hand” while the described technique uses feet. Preserve its wording and check whether this denotes manual work more generally.

Confirm whether ʕarnoṣe ʕəṣriwo at Jan 1.50/2341 specifically means tightening an already fitted muzzle or more general fastening. Does it extend to other gear? The proposed gloss is restricted to the attested muzzle context.
Confirm person/number and patient segmentation of ʕƏṣrənwanne at Jan 3.55/1551; no new morphological paradigm is inferred.
The relation between ʕṣr and ḥṣr 1 remains the round-1 editorial question.
Correct the article before Grasstaude
rationale: The accusative object is die Grasstaude; sie is a mistyped article. The supplied 57/176 translation also reads die Grasstaude.

summary: Wine/must and juice can stand as the extracted product object. This supports round 1’s product-metonymy observation; a new product-extraction sense is unnecessary.
Jan explicitly contrasts pressing by hands with pressing in sacks. This adds a clear means contrast to round 1’s hand-versus-foot question, without correcting any earlier source.
